nodes.name: HubSpot - Get deals
nodes.notes: Replace with n8n-nodes-base.hubspot node once the service key / core seat is confirmed. Requires scopes: crm.objects.deals.read, crm.objects.contacts.read, crm.schemas.deals.read, crm.objects.owners.read. Pagination follows HubSpot's paging.next.link cursor automatically, capped at 20 pages (2000 deals) - raise maxRequests if you have more.

nodes.name: HubSpot - Get pipelines
nodes.notes: Fetches all deal pipelines and their stages (id -> label) so raw dealstage IDs like 'qualifiedtobuy' or '1239370556' can be translated to human-readable stage names ('Qualified to Explore', 'Demo', etc.) that match the Content Grid. Requires crm.objects.deals.read (pipelines are covered by the same scope) - runs in parallel with the deals fetch, referenced by name inside 'Group by contact' rather than wired as a direct input.

nodes.name: Combine deals and pipelines
nodes.notes: Combines HubSpot - Get deals and HubSpot - Get pipelines into a single item list for ONE execution of Group by contact. Wiring both directly into the same input port (without this Merge node) causes n8n to run the downstream node separately per branch instead of combining them - this node prevents that.

nodes.name: Extract Global Rules
nodes.notes: Parses the 'Global Rules' tab into rows: { Rule, Detail }

nodes.name: Extract Content Grid
nodes.notes: Parses the 'Content Grid' tab into rows: { Product, Stage, Drip Week #, Variant Condition, Full-Block Copy (raw), One-Line Mention (raw), CTA, Dependency / Notes }

nodes.name: Extract Product Priority
nodes.notes: Parses the 'Product Priority' tab into rows: { Rank, Product, Notes }

nodes.name: Combine sheet tabs
nodes.notes: Combines rows from Global Rules, Content Grid, Product Priority, and Resource Links into one item list - Build content reference text below tells them apart by column shape.

nodes.name: Build content reference text
nodes.notes: Outputs ONE item: { referenceText }, including Global Rules, Product Priority, Content Grid, and Resource Links from the live workbook.

nodes.name: Filter to matching stages
nodes.notes: Drops deals whose stage isn't one of the 5 the Content Grid covers, and normalizes real HubSpot labels ('Demo Call', 'Due Diligence (IT, Legal, Compliance)') down to the spreadsheet's exact stage names. Contacts with zero remaining deals are dropped entirely - nothing to follow up on.

nodes.name: Collect contact IDs
nodes.notes: Runs once per batch from Loop Over Contacts (5 IDs at a time), well under HubSpot's 100-per-request cap. If you raise Loop Over Contacts' batchSize above 100, this call will start failing again - keep it at or below 100.

nodes.name: HubSpot - Get contact emails
nodes.notes: Batch contact read - requires crm.objects.contacts.read scope. Returns { results: [{ id, properties: { email } }] }.

nodes.name: Merge emails into contacts
nodes.notes: Contacts with no email on file get contactEmail: null - worth adding a filter downstream to skip those rather than sending to a null address.

nodes.name: Loop Over Contacts
nodes.notes: Processes contacts in small batches instead of firing all LLM/Gmail calls at once - avoids hitting the workflow timeout and Anthropic rate limits. Adjust batchSize as needed.

nodes.name: Extract draft email
nodes.notes: Bridges the LLM node's raw API response back to a flat { contactId, contactEmail, deals, draftEmail } shape per contact. Assumes responses stay in the same order/count as the batch from Loop Over Contacts - true for the normal path, but the single-item rejection-redraft loop will misalign here since it's 1 response vs a 5-item original batch; revisit if you build out the rejection loop further.

nodes.name: Generate approval token
nodes.notes: Creates a unique token per draft, used to look up this specific pending approval from the separate approval-webhook workflow.

nodes.name: Save pending draft
nodes.notes: REQUIRES MANUAL SETUP: create a Data Table named 'pending_approvals' first (columns: token, contactId, contactEmail, firstName, draftEmail, status, createdAt - all String except createdAt as Date), then open this node and re-select that table from the dataTableId dropdown (the placeholder value here won't resolve on its own). Also verify the column mapping matches after import - resource-mapper fields like this one are finicky to hand-author in raw JSON.

Match Product. * First look for RESOURCE LINKS rows whose Product exactly matches the selected CONTENT GRID Product. * A RESOURCE LINKS row with Product = "All Products" may be used only when its Used In rule applies. 2. Match the resource itself. * Match the resource named or clearly referenced by the CONTENT GRID wording to Resource Name. * Treat obvious wording variations as the same resource only when there is no ambiguity. * Examples: * "presentation deck" = "Presentation deck" * "pricing sheet" = "Pricing sheet" * "It Takes a Village blog" = "'It Takes a Village' blog" * "Father Ray's personal story" = "Father Ray's personal story blog" * "quote request form" = "Quote request form" 3. DEMO * Use rows whose Used In contains "Demo". * Resources with Used In = "Demo" apply to every Demo variant. * Resources with a population qualifier apply only to the matching CONTENT GRID Variant Condition. * "Demo — Population Age Pediatric" applies only to the Pediatric Demo variant. * "Demo — Population Age Adult" applies only to the Adult Demo variant. * A Mixed Demo variant may use both approved Pediatric and Adult resources when the CONTENT GRID explicitly requires both. DUE DILIGENCE * Use RESOURCE LINKS rows whose Used In contains "Due Diligence". * A resource whose Used In lists multiple stages, such as "Demo, Due Diligence", is valid for either listed stage.
